claim: The transcriptional complex Mondo/Max-like, MML-1/MXL-2, acts as a convergent transcriptional regulatory output of multiple longevity pathways in Caenorhabditis elegans.
source: The transcriptional complex Mondo/Max-like, MML-1/MXL-2, acts as a convergent transcriptional regulatory output of multiple longevity pathways in Caenorhabditis elegans.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known fact about the MML-1/MXL-2 complex.

claim: MondoA and ChREBP transcription factors coordinate nutrient sensing with carbohydrate and lipid metabolism across the evolutionary spectrum.
source: These transcription factors coordinate nutrient sensing with carbohydrate and lipid metabolism across the evolutionary spectrum.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge about these transcription factors.

claim: Knockdown of various glucose metabolic enzymes decreases MML-1 localization in the nucleus.
source: Here, we found that knockdown of various glucose metabolic enzymes decreases MML-1 localization in the nucleus
evidence: This is a primary finding from the RNAi screen presented in Figure 1A and B.

claim: Two hexokinase isozymes, hxk-1 and hxk-2, are the most vigorous regulators of MML-1 function.
source: identified two hexokinase isozymes, hxk-1 and hxk-2, as the most vigorous regulators of MML-1 function.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the RNAi screen shown in Figure 1.

claim: Upon hexokinase knockdown, MML-1 redistributes to mitochondria and lipid droplets.
source: Upon hexokinase knockdown, MML-1 redistributes to mitochondria and lipid droplets (LDs)
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by confocal microscopy data in Figures 2 and 4.

claim: Upon hexokinase knockdown, MML-1 transcriptional targets are downregulated.
source: Upon hexokinase knockdown, MML-1 redistributes to mitochondria and lipid droplets (LDs), and concomitantly, transcriptional targets are downregulated
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data showing decreased expression of MML-1 target genes in Figure 1E.

claim: Upon hexokinase knockdown, germline longevity is abolished.
source: Upon hexokinase knockdown, MML-1 redistributes to mitochondria and lipid droplets (LDs), and concomitantly, transcriptional targets are downregulated and germline longevity is abolished.
evidence: This is supported by lifespan data in Figure 1F showing that hxk-1 and hxk-2 knockdown suppress glp-1(e2141) longevity.

claim: hxk-1 regulates MML-1 through mitochondrial β-oxidation.
source: Further, we found that hxk-1 regulates MML-1 through mitochondrial β-oxidation
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2 showing that inhibition of β-oxidation rescues MML-1 nuclear localization under hxk-1 knockdown.

claim: hxk-2 regulates MML-1 by modulating the pentose phosphate pathway (PPP) and its coordinated association with LDs.
source: while hxk-2 regulates MML-1 by modulating the pentose phosphate pathway (PPP) and its coordinated association with LDs.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figures 3 and 4 showing that PPP inhibition rescues MML-1 function under hxk-2 knockdown and that MML-1 localizes to LDs.

claim: Inhibition of the PPP rescues mammalian MondoA nuclear translocation upon starvation.
source: Similarly, inhibition of the PPP rescues mammalian MondoA nuclear translocation and transcriptional function upon starvation.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 5 showing increased MondoA nuclear localization in HEK293T cells treated with 6-AN under starvation conditions.

claim: Inhibition of the PPP rescues mammalian MondoA transcriptional function upon starvation.
source: Similarly, inhibition of the PPP rescues mammalian MondoA nuclear translocation and transcriptional function upon starvation.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data in Figure 5D showing increased expression of MondoA target genes TXNIP and ARRDC4 upon 6-AN treatment.

claim: Aging is associated with dysregulation of gene expression and metabolism.
source: One key aspect of aging is the dysregulation of gene expression and metabolism (Fischer et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Fischer et al., 2022.

claim: Many transcription factors that regulate metabolic pathways control lifespan across the evolutionary spectrum.
source: Many transcription factors that regulate metabolic pathways have been shown to control lifespan in the evolutionary spectrum (Clancy et al., 2001; Green et al., 2022; Lapierre et al., 2013; Selman et al., 2008; Wang et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published studies.

claim: Changes in the activity of specific transcription factors impact gene expression patterns and alter metabolic processes, leading to a decline in cellular function and increased risk of age-related diseases.
source: Changes in the activity of specific transcription factors have been shown to impact gene expression patterns and alter metabolic processes, leading to a decline in cellular function and an increased risk of age-related diseases (Benhamed et al., 2012; Carroll et al., 2015; Denechaud et al., 2008; Du and Zheng, 2021; Tong et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published studies.

claim: MondoA and ChREBP are paralogous transcription factors that work in heterodimeric complexes with Max-like protein X (Mlx).
source: MondoA and the carbohydrate response element binding protein (ChREBP) are paralogous transcription factors that work in heterodimeric complexes with Max-like protein X (Mlx)
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about these transcription factors.

claim: MondoA and ChREBP have been identified as key regulators of glucose metabolism and energy homeostasis.
source: MondoA and the carbohydrate response element binding protein (ChREBP) are paralogous transcription factors that work in heterodimeric complexes with Max-like protein X (Mlx) and have been identified as key regulators of glucose metabolism and energy homeostasis.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about these transcription factors.

claim: MondoA and ChREBP recognize and bind hexanucleotide tandem sequences (CANNTG) in promoter regions called Enhancer box (E-box) sequences.
source: These transcription factors recognize and bind hexanucleotide tandem sequences (CANNTG) in the promoter regions called Enhancer box (E-box) sequences (Massari and Murre, 2000)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Massari and Murre, 2000.

claim: MondoA and ChREBP regulate genes involved in glucose uptake, utilization, and storage.
source: These transcription factors recognize and bind hexanucleotide tandem sequences (CANNTG) in the promoter regions called Enhancer box (E-box) sequences (Massari and Murre, 2000) of various genes involved in glucose uptake, utilization, and storage (Billin et al., 2000; Cha-Molstad et al., 2009; Sans et al., 2006; Stoltzman et al., 2008; Yamashita et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published studies.

claim: MondoA/ChREBP regulate lipid metabolism and cellular stress responses.
source: In addition to their role in glucose metabolism, MondoA/ChREBP has also been shown to regulate lipid metabolism and cellular stress responses (Iizuka et al., 2006; Ishii et al., 2004; Ma et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published studies.

claim: Changes in MondoA/ChREBP activity with age may contribute to age-related metabolic dysfunction, leading to a decline in glucose tolerance and increased risk of type 2 diabetes and obesity.
source: Studies have suggested that changes in MondoA/ChREBP activity with age may contribute to age-related metabolic dysfunction, leading to a decline in glucose tolerance and increased risk of type 2 diabetes and obesity (Ghasemi et al., 2015; Iizuka et al., 2006; Richards et al., 2017; Yamamoto-Imoto et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published studies.

claim: The transcriptional complex formed by MML-1 and MXL-2 is part of an integrated helix-loop-helix network required for lifespan extension in diverse longevity pathways.
source: In Caenorhabditis elegans, the transcriptional complex formed by MML-1 (MondoA/ChREBP homolog) and MXL-2 (Mlx homolog) is part of an integrated helix-loop-helix network required for lifespan extension in diverse longevity pathways (Johnson et al., 2014; Nakamura et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Johnson et al., 2014 and Nakamura et al., 2016.

claim: Knockdown of most enzymes involved in glycolysis decreased MML-1 nuclear accumulation.
source: Knockdown of most of the enzymes involved in glycolysis, as well as the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex, which links glycolysis to the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle via acetyl-CoA, decreased MML-1 nuclear accumulation (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the RNAi screen shown in Figure 1 and Supplementary file 1.

claim: Knockdown of the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex decreased MML-1 nuclear accumulation.
source: Knockdown of most of the enzymes involved in glycolysis, as well as the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex, which links glycolysis to the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle via acetyl-CoA, decreased MML-1 nuclear accumulation (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the RNAi screen shown in Figure 1 and Supplementary file 1.

claim: Knockdown of most enzymes in the TCA cycle decreased nuclear MML-1.
source: Interestingly, whereas most enzymes in the TCA cycle also decreased nuclear MML-1, inhibition of the oxoglutarate dehydrogenase complex (OGDC) subunits ogdh-1 and dld-1 and the succinyl-CoA synthase (SCS) suca-1 and sucg-1 subunits increased MML-1 nuclear localization.
evidence: This is a finding from the RNAi screen shown in Figure 1.

claim: Inhibition of the oxoglutarate dehydrogenase complex (OGDC) subunits ogdh-1 and dld-1 increased MML-1 nuclear localization.
source: Interestingly, whereas most enzymes in the TCA cycle also decreased nuclear MML-1, inhibition of the oxoglutarate dehydrogenase complex (OGDC) subunits ogdh-1 and dld-1 and the succinyl-CoA synthase (SCS) suca-1 and sucg-1 subunits increased MML-1 nuclear localization.
evidence: This is a finding from the RNAi screen shown in Figure 1.

claim: Inhibition of the succinyl-CoA synthase (SCS) suca-1 and sucg-1 subunits increased MML-1 nuclear localization.
source: Interestingly, whereas most enzymes in the TCA cycle also decreased nuclear MML-1, inhibition of the oxoglutarate dehydrogenase complex (OGDC) subunits ogdh-1 and dld-1 and the succinyl-CoA synthase (SCS) suca-1 and sucg-1 subunits increased MML-1 nuclear localization.
evidence: This is a finding from the RNAi screen shown in Figure 1.

claim: Knockdown of phosphogluconate dehydrogenase (PGDH) T25B9.9 triggered a strong increase in MML-1 nuclear accumulation.
source: We also observed that knockdown of enzymes involved in the oxidative and nonoxidative branches of the PPP, phosphogluconate dehydrogenase (PGDH) T25B9.9 and transketolase (TKT) tkt-1 genes, respectively, triggered a strong increase in MML-1 nuclear accumulation (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: This is a finding from the RNAi screen shown in Figure 1A and B.

claim: Knockdown of transketolase (TKT) tkt-1 triggered a strong increase in MML-1 nuclear accumulation.
source: We also observed that knockdown of enzymes involved in the oxidative and nonoxidative branches of the PPP, phosphogluconate dehydrogenase (PGDH) T25B9.9 and transketolase (TKT) tkt-1 genes, respectively, triggered a strong increase in MML-1 nuclear accumulation (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: This is a finding from the RNAi screen shown in Figure 1A and B.

claim: Overall changes in glucose metabolism regulate MML-1.
source: These data suggest that overall changes in glucose metabolism regulate MML-1 and that this transcription factor may sense the divergence of G6P to different branches of this network.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the RNAi screen data shown in Figure 1.

claim: MML-1 may sense the divergence of G6P to different branches of the glucose metabolism network.
source: These data suggest that overall changes in glucose metabolism regulate MML-1 and that this transcription factor may sense the divergence of G6P to different branches of this network.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the RNAi screen data.

claim: Among the three C. elegans hexokinase genes, hxk-1 and hxk-2 more strongly affected MML-1 nuclear localization than hxk-3.
source: Among the three C. elegans hexokinase genes, hxk-1 and hxk-2 more strongly affected MML-1 nuclear localization in two independent MML-1::GFP reporter strains (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), while hxk-3 had just a small effect on MML-1 nuclear localization
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: hxk-3 had just a small effect on MML-1 nuclear localization, probably due to its low expression in adult worms.
source: while hxk-3 had just a small effect on MML-1 nuclear localization, probably due to its low expression in adult worms (Hutter and Suh, 2016).
evidence: This is an interpretation supported by a citation to Hutter and Suh, 2016.

claim: 3-Bromopyruvate (3-BrP) is an alkylating agent and HKII inhibitor.
source: 3-Bromopyruvate (3-BrP) is an alkylating agent and HKII inhibitor
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the drug.

claim: 2-deoxy-glucose (2-DG) is an analog of glucose phosphorylated to 2-DG6P, which cannot be further metabolized, thus inhibiting hexokinase function.
source: 2-deoxy-glucose (2-DG) is an analog of glucose phosphorylated to 2-DG6P, which cannot be further metabolized, thus inhibiting hexokinase function.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the drug.

claim: Supplementation of 3-BrP significantly decreased MML-1 nuclear localization compared to control.
source: Supplementation of both drugs significantly decreased MML-1 nuclear localization compared to control (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and C)
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Supplementation of 2-DG significantly decreased MML-1 nuclear localization compared to control.
source: Supplementation of both drugs significantly decreased MML-1 nuclear localization compared to control (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and C)
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Hexokinase activity drives MML-1 nuclear translocation.
source: indicating that hexokinase activity drives MML-1 nuclear translocation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the pharmacological inhibition data.

claim: Each hexokinase RNAi was specific to each isozyme.
source: We used these strains to evaluate the protein levels by western blot (WB) and found that each RNAi was specific to each isozyme (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D and E).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D and E.

claim: hxk-1i and hxk-2i displayed no significant change in worm growth.
source: hxk-1i and hxk-2i displayed no significant change in worm growth, while hxk-3i-treated animals were somewhat smaller (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F and G).
evidence: This is supported by body size measurements in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F and G.

claim: hxk-3i-treated animals were somewhat smaller.
source: hxk-1i and hxk-2i displayed no significant change in worm growth, while hxk-3i-treated animals were somewhat smaller (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F and G).
evidence: This is supported by body size measurements in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F and G.

claim: Hexokinase knockdown did not affect pharyngeal pumping rate compared to control.
source: To determine if our observations were due to a change in food intake, we counted pharyngeal pumping rate but found no significant difference compared to the control (Figure 1—figure supplement 1H)
evidence: This is supported by pharyngeal pumping data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1H.

claim: Hexokinase knockdown did not affect worm motility compared to control.
source: nor did we see an effect on worm motility compared to control (Figure 1—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: This is supported by motility data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1I.

claim: Hexokinase knockdown did not affect the steady-state levels of mml-1 mRNA.
source: Moreover, hexokinase knockdown did not affect the steady-state levels of mml-1 mRNA (Figure 1—figure supplement 1J).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1J.

claim: The effects on MML-1 nuclear localization are not due to a decrease in food consumption or developmental phenotype.
source: Taken together, these data indicate no RNAi cross-reactivity among the hexokinase isozymes and that the effects on MML-1 nuclear localization are not due to a decrease in food consumption or developmental phenotype.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data on worm growth, pharyngeal pumping, and motility.

claim: MML-1 works in a transcriptional complex with MXL-2.
source: MML-1 works in a transcriptional complex with MXL-2
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: MML-1 and MXL-2 are required for lifespan extension in multiple longevity pathways, including germline-less glp-1(e2141) mutant.
source: previous studies have demonstrated that MML-1 and MXL-2 are required for lifespan extension in multiple longevity pathways, including germline-less glp-1(e2141) mutant (Nakamura et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Nakamura et al., 2016.

claim: MML-1 nuclear localization was increased in glp-1(e2141) as reported previously.
source: As expected, MML-1 nuclear localization was increased in glp-1(e2141) as reported previously (Nakamura et al., 2016)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Nakamura et al., 2016 and confirmed by data in Figure 1C and D.

claim: Upon hxk-1 and hxk-2 knockdown, MML-1 nuclear localization was abolished in glp-1(e2141) mutants.
source: upon hxk-1 and hxk-2 knockdown, MML-1 nuclear localization was abolished in glp-1(e2141) mutants (Figure 1C and D).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 1C and D.

claim: Expression of mdl-1, lgg-2, swt-1, and fat-5 decreased under hxk-1i and hxk-2i, but not under hxk-3i.
source: We observed decreased expression of mdl-1, lgg-2, swt-1, and fat-5 under hxk-1i and hxk-2i, but not under hxk-3i (Figure 1E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1K)
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data in Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1K.

claim: hxk-1i and hxk-2i significantly decreased glp-1(e2141) lifespan.
source: Accordingly, hxk-1i and hxk-2i significantly decreased glp-1(e2141) but did not affect wild-type lifespan (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is supported by lifespan data in Figure 1F.

claim: hxk-1i and hxk-2i did not affect wild-type lifespan.
source: Accordingly, hxk-1i and hxk-2i significantly decreased glp-1(e2141) but did not affect wild-type lifespan (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is supported by lifespan data in Figure 1F.

claim: Hexokinases are upstream regulators of MML-1 nuclear localization and transcriptional function in germline-mediated longevity.
source: These data indicate that hexokinases are upstream regulators of MML-1 nuclear localization and transcriptional function in germline-mediated longevity.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data on MML-1 localization, target gene expression, and lifespan in glp-1(e2141) mutants.

claim: In isp-1(qm150) mutants, hxk-1 and hxk-2 knockdown decreased MML-1 nuclear localization.
source: On the one hand, we observed that in isp-1(qm150) mutants, a model for mitochondrial longevity, hxk-1 and hxk-2 knockdown decreased MML-1 nuclear localization and abolished lifespan extension (Figure 1G and H).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 1G.

claim: In isp-1(qm150) mutants, hxk-1 and hxk-2 knockdown abolished lifespan extension.
source: On the one hand, we observed that in isp-1(qm150) mutants, a model for mitochondrial longevity, hxk-1 and hxk-2 knockdown decreased MML-1 nuclear localization and abolished lifespan extension (Figure 1G and H).
evidence: This is supported by lifespan data in Figure 1H.

claim: mml-1 was required for the insulin signaling daf-2(e1370) mutant longevity.
source: On the other hand, while mml-1 was required for the insulin signaling daf-2(e1370) mutant longevity, hxk-1 and hxk-2 knockdown did not alter MML-1 nuclear localization nor suppress the lifespan in this background (Figure 1—figure supplement 1L–M).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1L–M.

claim: hxk-1 and hxk-2 knockdown did not alter MML-1 nuclear localization in daf-2(e1370) mutants.
source: On the other hand, while mml-1 was required for the insulin signaling daf-2(e1370) mutant longevity, hxk-1 and hxk-2 knockdown did not alter MML-1 nuclear localization nor suppress the lifespan in this background (Figure 1—figure supplement 1L–M).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1L.

claim: hxk-1 and hxk-2 knockdown did not suppress the lifespan in daf-2(e1370) mutants.
source: On the other hand, while mml-1 was required for the insulin signaling daf-2(e1370) mutant longevity, hxk-1 and hxk-2 knockdown did not alter MML-1 nuclear localization nor suppress the lifespan in this background (Figure 1—figure supplement 1L–M).
evidence: This is supported by lifespan data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1M.

claim: MML-1 nuclear localization was increased in raga-1(ok701) mutants.
source: Further, we found that MML-1 nuclear localization was increased in raga-1(ok701) mutants, a model for mTORC1 longevity, and mml-1 was required for lifespan extension (Figure 1—figure supplement 1N and O).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1N.

claim: mml-1 was required for lifespan extension in raga-1(ok701) mutants.
source: Further, we found that MML-1 nuclear localization was increased in raga-1(ok701) mutants, a model for mTORC1 longevity, and mml-1 was required for lifespan extension (Figure 1—figure supplement 1N and O).
evidence: This is supported by lifespan data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1O.

claim: hxk-1 and hxk-2 knockdown did not suppress raga-1(ok701) longevity.
source: However, hxk-1 and hxk-2 knockdown did not suppress raga-1(ok701) longevity (Figure 1—figure supplement 1P).
evidence: This is supported by lifespan data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1P.

claim: While MML-1 acts as a convergent factor in four longevity pathways, it only requires HXK-1 and HXK-2 for germline and mitochondrial longevity, but not for insulin and mTOR longevity.
source: Collectively, these data suggest that while MML-1 acts as a convergent factor in these four longevity pathways, it only requires HXK-1 and HXK-2 for germline and mitochondrial longevity, but not for insulin and mTOR longevity.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data on MML-1 localization and lifespan in different longevity mutants.

claim: Mammals harbor four hexokinases that differ in tissue expression, subcellular localization, and affinity to glucose and G6P.
source: Mammals harbor four hexokinases that differ in tissue expression, subcellular localization, and affinity to glucose and G6P.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about mammalian hexokinases.

claim: HXK-1 was expressed in the cytosol of neurons, pharynx, gonadal sheath, and coelomocytes.
source: We found that HXK-1 was expressed in the cytosol of neurons, pharynx, gonadal sheath, and coelomocytes (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy data in Figure 2A.

claim: HXK-2 had a reticular expression pattern in neurons, muscle, intestine, and hypodermis.
source: HXK-2 had a reticular expression pattern in neurons, muscle, intestine, and hypodermis (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy data in Figure 2B.

claim: HXK-3 signal was diffused and highly expressed in the pharynx, muscle, hypodermis, and intestine.
source: HXK-3 signal was diffused and highly expressed in the pharynx, muscle, hypodermis, and intestine (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Full-length HXK-2 strongly co-localized with mitochondria.
source: Indeed, we observed that full-length HXK-2 strongly co-localized with mitochondria (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy data in Figure 2C.

claim: Mitochondrial localization of HXK-2 was abolished entirely in the d10 HXK-2 mutant that lacks the first 10 amino acids after the initiator methionine.
source: We also generated an HXK-2 mutant that lacks the first 10 amino acids after the initiator methionine (d10 HXK-2) and found that mitochondrial localization was abolished entirely (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy data in Figure 2C.

claim: Hexokinases are differentially expressed in C. elegans.
source: In summary, we found that hexokinases are differentially expressed in C. elegans and identified HXK-2 as the worm mitochondrial hexokinase.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the tissue expression data in Figure 2A, B, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: HXK-2 is the worm mitochondrial hexokinase.
source: In summary, we found that hexokinases are differentially expressed in C. elegans and identified HXK-2 as the worm mitochondrial hexokinase.
evidence: This is supported by co-localization data in Figure 2C.

claim: MML-1 localized with mitochondria in the intestine.
source: Hence, we crossed the MML-1::GFP strain with the mitochondrial reporter TOMM-20::mCherry under the intestinal promoter ges-1 and confirmed that MML-1 localized with mitochondria in the intestine (Figure 2D and E).
evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy data in Figure 2D and E.

claim: Under normal conditions, around 60–80% of the total MML-1 was nuclear, and 15% co-localized with mitochondria.
source: Under normal conditions, around 60–80% of the total MML-1 was nuclear, and 15% co-localized with mitochondria.
evidence: This is supported by co-localization analysis in Figure 2F.

claim: MML-1 mitochondrial localization was increased to ~62% of total MML-1 upon hxk-2i.
source: Interestingly, MML-1 mitochondrial localization was increased to ~62% of total MML-1 upon hxk-2i (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is supported by co-localization analysis in Figure 2F.

claim: Upon hxk-2 knockdown, MML-1 is excluded from the nucleus and re-localizes to a subset population of mitochondria.
source: Taken together, our data indicate that upon hxk-2 knockdown, MML-1 is excluded from the nucleus and re-localizes to a subset population of mitochondria.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the co-localization data in Figure 2D-F.

claim: Increased expression of hsp-6::GFP was observed upon knockdown of mitochondrial components ogdh-1, sucl-1, and sucl-2, as well as in control worms treated with antimycin A.
source: As expected, we observed increased expression of hsp-6::GFP, a reporter for mitochondrial stress, upon knockdown of mitochondrial components ogdh-1, sucl-1, and sucl-2, as well as in control worms treated with antimycin A (AA), a complex III inhibitor (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Inducing mitochondrial stress with AA did not affect MML-1 nuclear localization under control conditions and hxk-2 knockdown.
source: However, inducing mitochondrial stress with AA did not affect MML-1 nuclear localization under control conditions and hxk-2 knockdown (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Exposure to paraquat induced the oxidative reporter gst-4p::GFP.
source: We exposed worms to the ROS-generating compound paraquat and observed induction of the oxidative reporter gst-4p::GFP (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F)
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Exposure to paraquat did not affect MML-1 nuclear localization at the concentrations tested.
source: however, we did not see any effect on MML-1 nuclear localization at the concentrations tested (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1G.

claim: MML-1 regulation by glucose metabolism genes is independent of mitochondrial and oxidative stress.
source: Taken together, these data indicate that MML-1 regulation by glucose metabolism genes is independent of mitochondrial and oxidative stress.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data on mitochondrial stress and oxidative stress.

claim: Increased total lipid storage was observed under hexokinase knockdown in the wild-type and glp-1(e2141) backgrounds.
source: First, we measured the neutral lipid content by feeding the worms with the labeled fatty acid C1-BODIPY-C12 and found increased total lipid storage under hexokinase knockdown in the wild-type and glp-1(e2141) backgrounds (Figure 2—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1H.

claim: No difference in basal OCR was found under hxk-1, hxk-2, and mml-1 knockdown in the wild-type background.
source: We found no difference in basal OCR under hxk-1, hxk-2, and mml-1 knockdown in the wild-type background (Figure 2H).
evidence: This is supported by OCR data in Figure 2H.

claim: glp-1(e2141) animals showed decreased basal OCR compared to wild type.
source: glp-1(e2141) animals showed decreased basal OCR compared to wild type, whereas hxk-1 and mml-1 knockdown significantly increased the basal OCR compared to glp-1(e2141) (Figure 2H).
evidence: This is supported by OCR data in Figure 2H.

claim: hxk-1 and mml-1 knockdown significantly increased the basal OCR compared to glp-1(e2141).
source: glp-1(e2141) animals showed decreased basal OCR compared to wild type, whereas hxk-1 and mml-1 knockdown significantly increased the basal OCR compared to glp-1(e2141) (Figure 2H).
evidence: This is supported by OCR data in Figure 2H.

claim: A greater percentage of OCR reduction upon adding etomoxir was observed under hxk-1 knockdown in wild-type and hxk-1, hxk-2, and mml-1 knockdown in glp-1(e2141).
source: Interestingly, we saw a greater percentage of OCR reduction upon adding etomoxir under hxk-1 knockdown in wild-type and hxk-1, hxk-2, and mml-1 knockdown in glp-1(e2141) (Figure 2I), indicating higher mitochondrial β-oxidation levels.
evidence: This is supported by OCR data in Figure 2I.

claim: Higher mitochondrial β-oxidation levels were indicated under hxk-1 knockdown in wild-type and hxk-1, hxk-2, and mml-1 knockdown in glp-1(e2141).
source: Interestingly, we saw a greater percentage of OCR reduction upon adding etomoxir under hxk-1 knockdown in wild-type and hxk-1, hxk-2, and mml-1 knockdown in glp-1(e2141) (Figure 2I), indicating higher mitochondrial β-oxidation levels.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the OCR data in Figure 2I.

claim: Increased expression of acs-2p::GFP was found upon hxk-1 and hxk-2 knockdown.
source: We confirmed this result using the transcriptional reporter acs-2p::GFP, a mitochondrial acyl-CoA synthase that is induced and required for fatty acid β-oxidation in C. elegans (Van Gilst et al., 2005), and found increased expression upon hxk-1 and hxk-2 knockdown (Figure 2—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1I.

claim: MML-1 nuclear localization was rescued upon acs-2i under hxk-1i.
source: First, we performed a double knockdown of hxk-1 or hxk-2 combined with acs-2. MML-1 nuclear localization was rescued upon acs-2i under hxk-1i (Figure 2J).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2J.

claim: acs-2i did not rescue MML-1 nuclear localization under hxk-2i.
source: Interestingly, acs-2i did not rescue MML-1 nuclear localization under hxk-2i.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2J.

claim: Etomoxir supplementation rescued MML-1 nuclear localization under hxk-1i, but had no effect upon hxk-2i.
source: We also pharmacologically inhibited fatty acid oxidation by supplementing etomoxir and again saw the rescue of MML-1 nuclear localization under hxk-1i, but no effect upon hxk-2i (Figure 2K).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2K.

claim: HXK-1 normally promotes MML-1 nuclear localization by decreasing mitochondrial β-oxidation.
source: These data suggest that HXK-1 normally promotes MML-1 nuclear localization by decreasing mitochondrial β-oxidation and reveal that the two hexokinases might regulate MML-1 nuclear localization through somewhat independent pathways.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data on β-oxidation and MML-1 localization.

claim: The two hexokinases might regulate MML-1 nuclear localization through somewhat independent pathways.
source: These data suggest that HXK-1 normally promotes MML-1 nuclear localization by decreasing mitochondrial β-oxidation and reveal that the two hexokinases might regulate MML-1 nuclear localization through somewhat independent pathways.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the differential effects of β-oxidation inhibition on MML-1 localization under hxk-1i vs hxk-2i.

claim: Increased MML-1 nuclear localization was observed after supplementation with 1 mM of 6-AN.
source: In agreement with our previous results, we observed increased MML-1 nuclear localization after supplementation with 1 mM of 6-AN (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 3B.

claim: hxk-2i, but not hxk-1i, significantly increased the NADPH levels.
source: Moreover, we found that hxk-2i, but not hxk-1i, significantly increased the NADPH levels (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 3C.

claim: hxk-2i had increased TKT-1 enzymatic activity compared to the control.
source: Additionally, we found that hxk-2i had increased TKT-1 enzymatic activity compared to the control (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 3D.

claim: Inhibition of the mitochondrial hexokinase enhances the PPP.
source: These data suggest that inhibition of the mitochondrial hexokinase enhances the PPP.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the NADPH and TKT-1 activity data.

claim: Knocking down T25B9.9 and tkt-1 rescued MML-1 nuclear localization under hxk-2i.
source: Interestingly, knocking down these enzymes rescued MML-1 nuclear localization under hxk-2i (Figure 3E and F) but did not rescue the localization under hxk-1i (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 3E and F.

claim: Knocking down T25B9.9 and tkt-1 did not rescue MML-1 nuclear localization under hxk-1i.
source: Interestingly, knocking down these enzymes rescued MML-1 nuclear localization under hxk-2i (Figure 3E and F) but did not rescue the localization under hxk-1i (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Knocking down the PPP under hxk-2i rescued the expression of lgg-2, mdl-1, swt-1, and fat-5.
source: To evaluate MML-1 function, we measured its transcriptional readouts and found that knocking down the PPP under hxk-2i rescued the expression of lgg-2, mdl-1, swt-1, and fat-5 (Figure 3G, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B–D)
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data in Figure 3G and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B–D.

claim: Knocking down the PPP had no effect on MML-1 target gene expression under hxk-1i.
source: however, it had no effect under hxk-1i (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E–H).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E–H.

claim: Lower levels of G6P were observed upon double knockdown of hexokinases with T25B9.9 and tkt-1 compared to control.
source: Moreover, we observed lower levels of G6P upon double knockdown of hexokinases with T25B9.9 and tkt-1 compared to control (Figure 3H, Figure 3—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 3H and Figure 3—figure supplement 1I.

claim: The PPP activity is increased upon knockdown of the mitochondrial hexokinase HXK-2.
source: Taken together, these data suggest that the PPP activity is increased upon knockdown of the mitochondrial hexokinase HXK-2, and inhibiting the PPP is sufficient to rescue MML-1 function independent of G6P levels.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the NADPH, TKT-1 activity, and rescue data.

claim: Inhibiting the PPP is sufficient to rescue MML-1 function independent of G6P levels.
source: Taken together, these data suggest that the PPP activity is increased upon knockdown of the mitochondrial hexokinase HXK-2, and inhibiting the PPP is sufficient to rescue MML-1 function independent of G6P levels.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the rescue data showing that MML-1 function is restored despite low G6P levels.

claim: A significant lifespan extension was found upon tkt-1 knockdown in wild type.
source: As reported previously, we found a significant lifespan extension upon tkt-1 knockdown in wild type (Figure 3I).
evidence: This is supported by lifespan data in Figure 3I.

claim: Knockdown of the PPP in the glp-1(e2141) background had no additive effect on longevity.
source: Moreover, knockdown of the PPP in the glp-1(e2141) background had no additive effect on longevity, suggesting that glp-1 and tkt-1i may share common mechanisms in extending lifespan.
evidence: This is supported by lifespan data in Figure 3I.

claim: glp-1 and tkt-1i may share common mechanisms in extending lifespan.
source: Moreover, knockdown of the PPP in the glp-1(e2141) background had no additive effect on longevity, suggesting that glp-1 and tkt-1i may share common mechanisms in extending lifespan.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the lack of additive effect on longevity.

claim: Knockdown of T25B9.9 and tkt-1 rescued glp-1(e2141) longevity upon hxk-2i.
source: Consistent with our data, knockdown of T25B9.9 and tkt-1 rescued glp-1(e2141) longevity upon hxk-2i (Figure 3I, Figure 3—figure supplement 1J).
evidence: This is supported by lifespan data in Figure 3I and Figure 3—figure supplement 1J.

claim: An increase in the PPP under hxk-2 knockdown suppresses MML-1 function.
source: Collectively, these data indicate that an increase in the PPP under hxk-2 knockdown suppresses MML-1 function, and reducing PPP restores longer life, placing PPP epistatically downstream of hxk-2.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data on PPP activity, MML-1 function, and lifespan.

claim: Reducing PPP restores longer life, placing PPP epistatically downstream of hxk-2.
source: Collectively, these data indicate that an increase in the PPP under hxk-2 knockdown suppresses MML-1 function, and reducing PPP restores longer life, placing PPP epistatically downstream of hxk-2.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the epistasis data.

claim: MXL-2 was detected in the MML-1 immunoprecipitation.
source: We detected several proteins in the immunoprecipitation (IP), including MXL-2, an established MML-1 binding partner (Pickett et al., 2007; Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data in Figure 4A and a citation to Pickett et al., 2007.

claim: Analysis of the top 50 co-enriched candidates in MML-1 IPs revealed enrichment for nuclear and mitochondrial proteins.
source: Analysis of the top 50 co-enriched candidates in MML-1 IPs revealed enrichment for nuclear and mitochondrial proteins (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Multiple enriched proteins from different organelles, including LDs, were found in the MML-1 IP.
source: We also found multiple enriched proteins from different organelles, including LDs.
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data in Figure 4A.

claim: PLIN-1, one of the most abundant LD proteins, was co-enriched in MML-1 IP.
source: Interestingly, PLIN-1, one of the most abundant LD proteins, was co-enriched in MML-1 IP (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data in Figure 4A.

claim: All LipiBlue-stained structures were positive with the LD-resident proteins DHS-3::GFP and PLIN-1::mCherry.
source: First, we used LipiBlue, a dye to specifically visualize LD in vivo (Tatenaka et al., 2019), and found that all LipiBlue-stained structures were positive with the LD-resident proteins DHS-3::GFP and PLIN-1::mCherry (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D–F)
evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D–F.

claim: LipiBlue can be used as a reliable method for visualization of LD in C. elegans.
source: indicating that this dye could be used as a reliable method for visualization of LD in C. elegans.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the co-localization data with LD markers.

claim: MML-1 localized with LipiBlue-positive structures.
source: Next, we examined LipiBlue-stained animals co-expressing MML-1::GFP and TOMM-20::mCherry and saw that MML-1 localized with LipiBlue-positive structures (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy data in Figure 4C.

claim: MML-1 appeared localized to mitochondria associated with LD.
source: Interestingly, MML-1 appeared localized to mitochondria associated with LD (Figure 4C and D).
evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy data in Figure 4C and D.

claim: MML-1 co-localization with LDs was significantly increased upon hxk-2 knockdown.
source: Moreover, this co-localization was significantly increased upon hxk-2 knockdown (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by co-localization analysis in Figure 4E.

claim: Inhibition of transaldolase and enzymes from the PPP has been shown to activate a fasting-like response by increasing lipolysis and enhancing the breakdown of LD.
source: Inhibition of transaldolase and enzymes from the PPP has been shown to activate a fasting-like response by increasing lipolysis and enhancing the breakdown of LD (Bennett et al., 2017), including higher expression of the adipose triglyceride lipase ATGL-1 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Bennett et al., 2017 and data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1G.

claim: A significant reduction in diameter and the total amount of LDs was observed upon knockdown of tkt-1.
source: We observed a significant reduction in diameter and the total amount of LDs upon knockdown of tkt-1, while hxk-2i did not have an effect (Figure 4F, Figure 4—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1H.

claim: hxk-2i did not have an effect on LD size.
source: We observed a significant reduction in diameter and the total amount of LDs upon knockdown of tkt-1, while hxk-2i did not have an effect (Figure 4F, Figure 4—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1H.

claim: Double knockdown of hxk-2 and tkt-1 resulted in smaller and fewer LDs than the control.
source: Double knockdown of hxk-2 and tkt-1, however, resulted in smaller and fewer LDs than the control.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1H.

claim: Knockdown of acs-2i and hxk-1i acs-2i double knockdown resulted in a mild but significant increase in LD size.
source: Interestingly, we found that knockdown of acs-2i and hxk-1i acs-2i double knockdown resulted in a mild but significant increase in LD size (Figure 4—figure supplement 1I)
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1I.

claim: The two hexokinases regulate MML-1 via distinct mechanisms.
source: supporting the notion that the two hexokinases regulate MML-1 via distinct mechanisms.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the differential effects on LD size.

claim: MML-1 can localize with a specific subpopulation of mitochondria associated with LD.
source: Collectively, these data suggest that MML-1 can localize with a specific subpopulation of mitochondria associated with LD and that inhibition of the PPP can rescue MML-1 nuclear localization upon hxk-2i correlated with decreasing LD size.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the co-localization and LD size data.

claim: Inhibition of the PPP can rescue MML-1 nuclear localization upon hxk-2i correlated with decreasing LD size.
source: Collectively, these data suggest that MML-1 can localize with a specific subpopulation of mitochondria associated with LD and that inhibition of the PPP can rescue MML-1 nuclear localization upon hxk-2i correlated with decreasing LD size.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the rescue and LD size data.

claim: atgl-1i increased lipid levels while dgat-2i worms did not show significant changes under ad libitum conditions.
source: First, we measured the neutral lipid composition and found that atgl-1i increased lipid levels while dgat-2i worms did not show significant changes under ad libitum conditions (Figure 4—figure supplement 1J).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1J.

claim: dgat-2i increased MML-1 nuclear localization.
source: Next, we tested MML-1 nuclear localization and observed that dgat-2i increased MML-1 nuclear localization while atgl-1i resulted in decreased levels of nuclear MML-1 (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 4G.

claim: atgl-1i resulted in decreased levels of nuclear MML-1.
source: Next, we tested MML-1 nuclear localization and observed that dgat-2i increased MML-1 nuclear localization while atgl-1i resulted in decreased levels of nuclear MML-1 (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 4G.

claim: MML-1 nuclear localization in atgl-1i was rescued upon tkt-1 knockdown.
source: Finally, we did an epistatic analysis of LD metabolism and the PPP and found that MML-1 nuclear localization in atgl-1i was rescued upon tkt-1 knockdown (Figure 4H)
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 4H.

claim: LD metabolism is upstream or parallel to the PPP in MML-1 regulation.
source: thus suggesting that LD metabolism is upstream or parallel to the PPP in MML-1 regulation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the epistasis data.

claim: Decreased NADPH/NADP+ ratio was observed in HEK293T cells treated with 6-AN and under starvation conditions.
source: First, we observed decreased NADPH/NADP+ ratio in cells treated with 6-AN and under starvation conditions (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: In both high-glucose and starvation conditions, MondoA nuclear localization was increased upon inhibition of the PPP.
source: Next, we found that in both conditions, MondoA nuclear localization was increased upon inhibition of the PPP (Figure 5A and B)
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 5A and B.

claim: There was no evident regulation of MondoA at the transcript level upon PPP inhibition.
source: while there was no evident regulation of MondoA at the transcript level (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data in Figure 5C.

claim: Increased expression of TXNIP and ARRDC4 was observed upon PPP inhibition, consistent with MondoA increased nuclear localization.
source: Consistent with MondoA increased nuclear localization, we observed increased expression of two of the best-described downstream targets of MondoA, TXNIP and ARRDC4 (Figure 5D, Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data in Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The PPP regulates mammalian MondoA localization and transcriptional function.
source: These findings indicate that the PPP regulates mammalian MondoA localization and transcriptional function.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data on MondoA localization and target gene expression in HEK293T cells.

claim: MondoA localization reportedly responds to glucose 6-phosphate (G6P) and other hexose phosphate sugars in cultured cells by translocating to the nucleus and regulating the expression of its downstream targets.
source: MondoA reportedly responds to glucose 6-phosphate (G6P) and other hexose phosphate sugars in cultured cells by translocating to the nucleus and regulating the expression of its downstream targets (Stoltzman et al., 2008; Stoltzman et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Stoltzman et al., 2008 and Stoltzman et al., 2011.

claim: Human HKI and HKII have been shown to bind reversibly to the mitochondria.
source: Human HKI and HKII have been shown to bind reversibly to the mitochondria (Sui and Wilson, 1997).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Sui and Wilson, 1997.

claim: Binding of hexokinase to mitochondria depends on an intrinsic hydrophobic N-terminal sequence critical for inserting into the outer mitochondrial membrane.
source: Binding depends on an intrinsic hydrophobic N-terminal sequence critical for inserting into the outer mitochondrial membrane (Pastorino et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Pastorino et al., 2002.

claim: Mitochondria and LDs physically interact with one another to regulate metabolism.
source: Mitochondria and LDs physically interact with one another to regulate metabolism (Boutant et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Boutant et al., 2017.

claim: Both PLIN1/PLIN-1 and ACSL1/ACS-13 have been proposed to tether mitochondria and LD.
source: Although the proteins involved in these contact sites are just beginning to be uncovered, both PLIN1/PLIN-1 and ACSL1/ACS-13 have been proposed to tether mitochondria and LD (Gordaliza-Alaguero et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Gordaliza-Alaguero et al., 2019.

claim: MondoA was previously seen in large-scale proteomics associated with LD.
source: MondoA was previously seen in large-scale proteomics associated with LD (Krahmer et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Krahmer et al., 2018.

claim: MondoA and Mlx localized with LD through amphipathic helices in the C-terminus in SUM159 cells.
source: It was shown that MondoA and Mlx localized with LD through amphipathic helices in the C-terminus in SUM159 cells (Mejhert et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Mejhert et al., 2020.

claim: MondoA/Mlx co-localization with LD inhibits its transcriptional activity, limiting glucose-dependent transcription.
source: The researchers proposed a model in which MondoA/Mlx co-localization with LD inhibits its transcriptional activity, limiting glucose-dependent transcription.
evidence: This is a model proposed by Mejhert et al., 2020.
